feasibility.buildNote: cleanBuildSec and incrementalRebuildSec measure the single-tree freeze build; the evaluator builds candidate and reference trees in each eval
feasibility.evalSecNote: mean containerized eval wall across the two admission ordering passes (122.4 and 113.3 averaged over 14 evals each); includes the candidate plus in-eval reference harness builds and 12 bench repetitions per workload

measurement.benchSampling: per workload: pristine in-eval reference and candidate bench legs interleaved on the same trusted per-iteration token stream, one warm repetition each, five timed repetitions with each phase scored from its minimum nanoseconds for candidate and reference alike. The trusted Python parent owns the clock: per timed iteration it streams an opaque mutation seed, waits for the leg to finish untimed prep, then times only the parse from releasing an opaque parse-go token to the leg's post-parse echo of it (mutation, base-tree construction, digesting and cleanup are never on the clock, and the candidate-linked harness holds no clock to rewrite); every timed tree's full pre-order signature digest must equal the pristine reference run on the identical token stream. Each leg runs in a fresh IPC namespace with fresh /var/tmp and /dev/shm tmpfs, and the full candidate-uid process tree is reaped after every reference and candidate leg. Score is the frozen scale 50661657.83045164 times the geometric mean of the 12 per-cell reference/candidate minimum-time ratios.
measurement.platform: linux/arm64 Docker Desktop on Apple M3 Max
